title: Daejeon's AI care robot Kkumdori hears a woman in her 70s, alone at 2 a.m., repeat “I want to die” and “save me”; its alert brings police and a hospital admission
summary: Daejeon's Kkumdori care robot, built on ChatGPT 4.0, flagged a woman in her 70s saying “I want to die” at 2 a.m. on 6 August 2025; police came, and a hospital admitted her the next day.
account: The supplier Mr. Mind announced on 14 January 2025 that it would provide the 1,000 robots of the 2025 program. They are its 4.0 model, with conversation based on ChatGPT 4.0. At about 2 a.m. on 6 August 2025, a woman in her 70s identified as “A” was at home in Deogam-dong, Daedeok-gu, Daejeon, South Korea. She lives alone and has schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. She repeatedly told the city-issued AI care robot Kkumdori “I want to die” and “save me”. The robot's crisis-detection algorithm flagged the words and alerted the operator's control center. A staff member phoned her. When she kept repeating them, staff reported to police on 112 with her location. Officers found her emotionally unstable and contacted her family. Police judged hospital treatment urgent. On the afternoon of 7 August she was admitted with her guardian's consent. Daejeon announced the case on 13 August 2025. On 10 September 2025 Daejon Ilbo reported that two users that it interviewed value the robot as company. The paper also reported that the city acknowledges a gap in use between men and women. Yonhap reported on 1 August 2026 that Daejeon's 1,000 care robots remain in service.
purpose: Daejeon issued 1,000 Kkumdori robots from January 2025, 200 per district, under its community integrated-care project. They went to elderly, disabled and low-income people living alone. They offer companionship, medication and schedule reminders and health monitoring. They detect crisis signs such as suicide risk and depression and automatically notify agencies and guardians. The alert was that function.
system: AI care robot 'Kkumdori' (AI 돌봄로봇 꿈돌이), a conversational companion robot in the shape of Daejeon's mascot, with a crisis-detection algorithm linked to a 24-hour control center
model_version: Mr. Mind (미스터마인드) 4.0 model, with two-way conversation based on ChatGPT 4.0, supplied for the 2025 Daejeon program
developer: Not named in the 2025 reports, which say only '해당 업체' (the company) runs the control system; the 2022 pilot robots in the same mascot form were supplied by Mr. Mind (미스터마인드) under an MOU with Daejeon (ZDNet Korea, 5 April 2022)
deployer: Daejeon Metropolitan City (대전시), Daejeon-style community integrated care project, with the supplier's control center
domain: Social welfare (home care for people living alone)
taxonomy_note: A suicide intervention; Trustible's only health type is physical health.

ratings.reason: A woman in her 70s living alone, with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, was in acute crisis at 2 a.m. She got a check-in call, a police visit that night and protective hospital admission the next afternoon. The city and the headlines call it life-saving. No attempt was reported, so the counterfactual is unproven. Her guardian said that having the robot beside her had been a great support to her.

The sources report no time, cost or capability that the city welfare office gained from this case. Its director cited the case as a model and the city kept the program, and neither of these is a realized outcome for the office.

ai_role.statement: The robot's crisis-detection algorithm recognized repeated danger words (“죽고 싶다”, “살려줘”) in conversation at 2 a.m. It sent an alert to a human control center. People did everything after that: the check-in call, the 112 report with location, the police visit, the family contact and the admission. The city's welfare director says the alert is what made the rapid dispatch and protection possible. Whether A would have come to harm that night is not established. Every account derives from the city's 13 August briefing.

produced_by: A municipal program that put conversational robots with a crisis-word detection algorithm into 1,000 homes of people living alone, 200 per district, from January 2025.
A 24-hour human control center run by the supplier that receives alerts, phones the resident, and reports to police (112) with the location.
A resident who habitually talked, sang and danced with the robot, so her statements at 2 a.m. were spoken aloud to it.
Police able to attend at night, and a family and hospital able to complete a protective admission the next day.
must_hold: Alerts go to humans who act at night. The robot itself does nothing beyond detecting words and raising the alarm.
The detection catches explicit statements (“죽고 싶다”, “살려줘”). A silent crisis would not trigger it.
Residents keep talking to the device. Her guardian said it was a great support to her.

echoes.setting: Yonhap, 1 August 2026: at about midnight on 20 July 2026 an 80-something in Daejeon's Seo-gu with severe abdominal pain told the care robot to call 119; the control center relayed it, paramedics arrived at about 00:30 and took the person to hospital (https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20260731144200063).
Yonhap, 1 August 2026: in November 2025 an 80-something in Daedeok-gu, badly hurt after falling from bed, called “Aria, help me” to an AI speaker at home and was rescued by 119 (same article).

Daejeon, the same program: a man in his 50s with terminal liver cancer, living alone, was skipping meals. Kkumdori flagged warning signs, and welfare officials visited and arranged meal support (Daejon Ilbo, 10 September 2025).

Daejeon: a woman in her 80s fell at home and could not move. She called for help to an AI speaker, the control center called 119 and she was taken to hospital. Daejeon MBC reported the case on 20 November 2025 without giving its date.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. Filed as protective response with prevention unproven rather than the classifier's specific harm prevented: the protective chain (alert, check-in call, 112 report, police visit, next-day admission) is documented by many outlets quoting the city's 13 August 2025 briefing and its welfare director Kim Jong-min, but no attempt was reported and nothing shows what would have happened without the alert. The Monitor's “70-year-old” renders “70대” (in her 70s); Hankyung and Kookmin Ilbo say a woman and her guardian calls her “할머니”, so one outlet's auto-summary “남성” was discarded. Money Today adds Deogam-dong. The supplier is unnamed in 2025 reports; ZDNet Korea (2022) records Mr. Mind's MOU for the pilot robots in the same mascot form, which may or may not cover the 2025 batch. No city press release could be retrieved (daejeon.go.kr returned an error page).
Benefit type set to Improved Physical Health under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Accessibility among the six first used.
Added what happened since from the cited sources.
Country of the deployer added from the organization's own site or a registry.
Prose pass: a rating reason, account, purpose, the replication conditions, the system's part rewritten in shorter sentences with abbreviations expanded; facts, figures and quotations unchanged.

Added one source, an independent one; dated the record to 6 August 2025 (observed); recorded what the benefit is measured against; named the model version; recorded two other attempts to repeat the benefit.
Edited the headline, summary, account of events for accuracy and clarity; corrected how the cited sources are classified; revised the depth ratings.

data.retained_case_account: At about 2 a.m. on 6 August 2025, a woman in her 70s identified as “A” was at home in Deogam-dong, Daedeok-gu, Daejeon, South Korea. She lives alone and has schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. She repeatedly told the city-issued AI care robot Kkumdori “I want to die” and “save me”. The robot's crisis-detection algorithm flagged the words and alerted the operator's control center. A staff member phoned her. When she kept repeating them, staff reported to police on 112 with her location. Officers found her emotionally unstable and contacted her family. Police judged hospital treatment urgent. On the afternoon of 7 August she was admitted with her guardian's consent. Daejeon announced the case on 13 August 2025.

retained_ai_contribution_statement.statement: The robot's crisis-detection algorithm recognized repeated danger words (“죽고 싶다”, “살려줘”) in conversation at 2 a.m. It sent an alert to a human control center. People did everything after that: the check-in call, the 112 report with location, the police visit, the family contact and the admission. The city's welfare director says the alert is what made the rapid dispatch and protection possible. Whether A would have come to harm that night is not established. Every account derives from the city's 13 August briefing.

fields.account: The supplier Mr. Mind announced on 14 January 2025 that it would provide the 1,000 robots of the 2025 program. They are its 4.0 model, with conversation based on ChatGPT 4.0. At about 2 a.m. on 6 August 2025, a woman in her 70s identified as “A” was at home in Deogam-dong, Daedeok-gu, Daejeon, South Korea. She lives alone and has schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. She repeatedly told the city-issued AI care robot Kkumdori “I want to die” and “save me”. The robot's crisis-detection algorithm flagged the words and alerted the operator's control center. A staff member phoned her. When she kept repeating them, staff reported to police on 112 with her location. Officers found her emotionally unstable and contacted her family. Police judged hospital treatment urgent. On the afternoon of 7 August she was admitted with her guardian's consent. Daejeon announced the case on 13 August 2025. On 10 September 2025 Daejon Ilbo reported that two users that it interviewed value the robot as company. The paper also reported that the city acknowledges a gap in use between men and women. Yonhap reported on 1 August 2026 that Daejeon's 1,000 care robots remain in service.

ratings.reason: A woman in her 70s living alone, with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, was in acute crisis at 2 a.m. She got a check-in call, a police visit that night and protective hospital admission the next afternoon. The city and the headlines call it life-saving. No attempt was reported, so the counterfactual is unproven. Her guardian said that having the robot beside her had been a great support to her.

The sources report no time, cost or capability that the city welfare office gained from this case. Its director cited the case as a model and the city kept the program, and neither of these is a realized outcome for the office.

fields.purpose: Daejeon issued 1,000 Kkumdori robots from January 2025, 200 per district, under its community integrated-care project. They went to elderly, disabled and low-income people living alone. They offer companionship, medication and schedule reminders and health monitoring. They detect crisis signs such as suicide risk and depression and automatically notify agencies and guardians. The alert was that function.

produced_by: A municipal program that put conversational robots with a crisis-word detection algorithm into 1,000 homes of people living alone, 200 per district, from January 2025.
A 24-hour human control center run by the supplier that receives alerts, phones the resident, and reports to police (112) with the location.
A resident who habitually talked, sang and danced with the robot, so her statements at 2 a.m. were spoken aloud to it.
Police able to attend at night, and a family and hospital able to complete a protective admission the next day.
must_hold: Alerts go to humans who act at night. The robot itself does nothing beyond detecting words and raising the alarm.
The detection catches explicit statements (“죽고 싶다”, “살려줘”). A silent crisis would not trigger it.
Residents keep talking to the device. Her guardian said it was a great support to her.

Yonhap, 1 August 2026: in November 2025 an 80-something in Daedeok-gu, badly hurt after falling from bed, called “Aria, help me” to an AI speaker at home and was rescued by 119 (same article).

Daejeon, the same program: a man in his 50s with terminal liver cancer, living alone, was skipping meals. Kkumdori flagged warning signs, and welfare officials visited and arranged meal support (Daejon Ilbo, 10 September 2025).

Daejeon: a woman in her 80s fell at home and could not move. She called for help to an AI speaker, the control center called 119 and she was taken to hospital. Daejeon MBC reported the case on 20 November 2025 without giving its date.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. Filed as protective response with prevention unproven rather than the classifier's specific harm prevented: the protective chain (alert, check-in call, 112 report, police visit, next-day admission) is documented by many outlets quoting the city's 13 August 2025 briefing and its welfare director Kim Jong-min, but no attempt was reported and nothing shows what would have happened without the alert. The Monitor's “70-year-old” renders “70대” (in her 70s); Hankyung and Kookmin Ilbo say a woman and her guardian calls her “할머니”, so one outlet's auto-summary “남성” was discarded. Money Today adds Deogam-dong. The supplier is unnamed in 2025 reports; ZDNet Korea (2022) records Mr. Mind's MOU for the pilot robots in the same mascot form, which may or may not cover the 2025 batch. No city press release could be retrieved (daejeon.go.kr returned an error page).
Benefit type set to Improved Physical Health under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Accessibility among the six first used.
Added what happened since from the cited sources.

display.answer: Most reports restate the city's announcement of 13 August 2025. Daejon Ilbo restated it on 10 September 2025 and added its own interviews with two robot users. Yonhap recounted the case again on 1 August 2026.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: Daejeon's Kkumdori care robot, built on ChatGPT 4.0, flagged a woman in her 70s saying “I want to die” at 2 a.m. on 6 August 2025; police came, and a hospital admitted her the next day.
fields.account: The supplier Mr. Mind announced on 14 January 2025 that it would provide the 1,000 robots of the 2025 program. They are its 4.0 model, with conversation based on ChatGPT 4.0. At about 2 a.m. on 6 August 2025, a woman in her 70s identified as “A” was at home in Deogam-dong, Daedeok-gu, Daejeon, South Korea. She lives alone and has schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. She repeatedly told the city-issued AI care robot Kkumdori “I want to die” and “save me”. The robot's crisis-detection algorithm flagged the words and alerted the operator's control center. A staff member phoned her. When she kept repeating them, staff reported to police on 112 with her location. Officers found her emotionally unstable and contacted her family. Police judged hospital treatment urgent. On the afternoon of 7 August she was admitted with her guardian's consent. Daejeon announced the case on 13 August 2025. On 10 September 2025 Daejon Ilbo reported that two users that it interviewed value the robot as company. The paper also reported that the city acknowledges a gap in use between men and women. Yonhap reported on 1 August 2026 that Daejeon's 1,000 care robots remain in service.

produced_by: A municipal program that put conversational robots with a crisis-word detection algorithm into 1,000 homes of people living alone, 200 per district, from January 2025.
A 24-hour human control center run by the supplier that receives alerts, phones the resident, and reports to police (112) with the location.
A resident who habitually talked, sang and danced with the robot, so her statements at 2 a.m. were spoken aloud to it.
Police able to attend at night, and a family and hospital able to complete a protective admission the next day.
must_hold: Alerts go to humans who act at night. The robot itself does nothing beyond detecting words and raising the alarm.
The detection catches explicit statements (“죽고 싶다”, “살려줘”). A silent crisis would not trigger it.
Residents keep talking to the device. Her guardian said it was a great support to her.

echoes.setting: Yonhap, 1 August 2026: at about midnight on 20 July 2026 an 80-something in Daejeon's Seo-gu with severe abdominal pain told the care robot to call 119; the control center relayed it, paramedics arrived at about 00:30 and took the person to hospital (https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20260731144200063).
Yonhap, 1 August 2026: in November 2025 an 80-something in Daedeok-gu, badly hurt after falling from bed, called “Aria, help me” to an AI speaker at home and was rescued by 119 (same article).

Daejeon, the same program: a man in his 50s with terminal liver cancer, living alone, was skipping meals. Kkumdori flagged warning signs, and welfare officials visited and arranged meal support (Daejon Ilbo, 10 September 2025).

Daejeon: a woman in her 80s fell at home and could not move. She called for help to an AI speaker, the control center called 119 and she was taken to hospital. Daejeon MBC reported the case on 20 November 2025 without giving its date.
